body:
I ran a probe with 9 cases (an SVG text control, not shown, printed sharp everywhere) in Chrome, Firefox and Safari and printed each to PDF. Each canvas is 20×10 px shown at 160×80 CSS px, shows "A" at load, and some cases draw "B" at print time. "sharp" means the letter is text in the PDF, "pixelated" means it is an embedded 20×10 image.

| Case (print-time drawing) | Chrome Canary 159.0.8153.0 | Firefox Nightly 162.0a1 | Safari TP 256 (22627.1.6.3) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | A, pixelated | A, pixelated | A, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: `clearRect` whole canvas, then B | **B, sharp** | B, pixelated | B, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: B only, no clear | A+B, pixelated | A+B, pixelated | A+B, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: `fillRect` whole canvas, then B | B, pixelated | B, pixelated | B, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: `clearRect`, B, then `putImageData` | B, pixelated | B, pixelated | B, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: `clearRect`, then B, `image-rendering: pixelated` | B, pixelated | B, pixelated | B, pixelated |
| `beforeprint`: `reset()`, then B | **B, sharp** | B, pixelated | B, pixelated |
| `mozPrintCallback`: `clearRect`, then B | A, pixelated | **B, sharp** | A, pixelated |

So a page gets vector output in Chromium only if it wipes the canvas with `clearRect` or `reset()` before redrawing; painting it over with `fillRect` is not enough. Correction to the description above: `fillRect` does not count as a full clear.

Probe and PDFs: 

[run-2026-11-10-safari-tp-256-22627.1.6.3-canvas-print-vector.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34604668/run-2026-11-10-safari-tp-256-22627.1.6.3-canvas-print-vector.pdf)
[run-2026-11-10-firefox-nightly-162.0a1-canvas-print-vector.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34604666/run-2026-11-10-firefox-nightly-162.0a1-canvas-print-vector.pdf)
[run-2026-11-10-chrome-canary-159.0.8153.0-canvas-print-vector.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34604667/run-2026-11-10-chrome-canary-159.0.8153.0-canvas-print-vector.pdf)
[probe-canvas-print-vector.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34604665/probe-canvas-print-vector.html)

A few answers come to mind, though note I cannot officially represent Chromium:
1. I believe replayed draw ops should be allowed if that is possible given the other choices we make.
2. I prefer explicit opt-in in situations like this. I presume Mozilla feel the same way. The op-in could even take something that indicates the print resolution, allowing for a backing store sized correctly, or at least an integer scale.
3. Implicit seems bad.
4. Some preferred resolution information in an explicit method could address this.
5. Outside my wheelhouse.
